record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
record.original_question: Let G be a Hausdorff semitopological group, meaning that G is a group with a topology such that multiplication is separately continuous and inversion is continuous. If the underlying topological space of G is Baire, must G be a topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a triple $(G,\cdot,\tau)$ a Hausdorff semitopological group with continuous inversion if $G$ is a group, $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $G$, the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto x\cdot y$, is separately continuous (i.e., continuous in each variable when the other is fixed), and the inversion map $G\to G$, $x\mapsto x^{-1}$, is continuous. Recall that a topological space is Baire if the intersection of any countable family of dense open subsets is dense, and that $(G,\cdot,\tau)$ is a topological group if, in addition to continuous inversion, the multiplication map is jointly continuous as a map $G\times G\to G$.

Question: Must every Hausdorff semitopological group with continuous inversion whose underlying topological space is Baire be a topological group?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal an active line of research giving partial positive results (e.g., every Čech-analytic Baire semitopological group is a topological group; metrizable Baire and various Bouziad-type conditions imply the conclusion) and counterexamples in weaker settings (a separable Baire semi-metric semitopological group that is not paratopological), but no source clearly settles the general question for Hausdorff semitopological groups with continuous inversion that are Baire. The problem appears to still be considered open.

status_evidence.title: Semitopological groups, Bouziad spaces and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies conditions (Bouziad-type, Čech-analytic Baire) under which a semitopological group is a topological group.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results are known under additional completeness/Baire-type hypotheses, but the general Baire case is not asserted to be solved.

status_evidence.title: Separate and Joint Continuity in Baire Groups (Z. Piotrowski)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on automatic joint continuity in Baire semitopological groups.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of automatic joint continuity in Baire semitopological groups is treated as a guiding open question with only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Classes of Baire spaces defined by topological games
status_evidence.snippet: Develops further sufficient conditions on Baire-like semitopological groups to be topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research effort indicates the general question remains unresolved.
